operations.title: Classic Lemon Hummus
operations.subtitle: Smooth, bright, ready in ten minutes
operations.description: A pantry-staple hummus with plenty of lemon and a good glug of olive oil. Doubles easily.

instructions.title: Blitz
instructions.instruction: Combine chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin and salt in a food processor. Blend until crumbly.

instructions.title: Emulsify
instructions.instruction: With the motor running, stream in the olive oil and 2–4 tablespoons of cold water until silky. Taste and adjust lemon and salt.

instructions.title: Serve
instructions.instruction: Spoon into a bowl, swirl the top, and finish with olive oil and a pinch of cumin.

operations.notes: Keeps a week in the fridge. Loosens up with a splash of water after chilling.
operations.eoeNotes: Smooth texture — generally easy for EoE; check tolerance for sesame (tahini).
operations.bloodSugarNotes: Low glycemic; pair with vegetables rather than bread to keep it gentle.
operations.antiInflammatoryNotes: Olive oil, chickpeas and garlic are all anti-inflammatory staples.
operations.storage: Airtight container in the fridge, up to 7 days.
operations.freezer: Freezes fine for 3 months; stir well after thawing.
operations.reheating: Serve cold or at room temperature.

operations.title: Three-Bean Garden Chili
operations.subtitle: A big, freezer-friendly pot
operations.description: Hearty vegan chili built for batch cooking — sweet with garden tomatoes and squash, warm with cumin and smoked paprika.

ingredients.name: crushed tomatoes
ingredients.notes: one large can, or 1 kg fresh

instructions.title: Soften
instructions.instruction: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook onion, garlic and peppers until soft, about 8 minutes.

instructions.title: Bloom the spices
instructions.instruction: Stir in chili powder, cumin and paprika; cook 1 minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer
instructions.instruction: Add tomatoes, all the beans, zucchini if using, and a cup of water. Simmer uncovered 35 minutes, stirring now and then.

instructions.title: Season and rest
instructions.instruction: Salt to taste. Like most chilis, it is even better the next day.

operations.notes: Serve over rice, baked potatoes, or on its own with cornbread.
operations.bloodSugarNotes: High fibre and plant protein keep this very blood-sugar friendly.
operations.antiInflammatoryNotes: Beans, tomatoes, garlic and spices — solidly anti-inflammatory.
operations.freezer: Portion into containers; freezes beautifully for 6 months.
operations.reheating: Reheat gently on the stove with a splash of water.

operations.title: Roasted Squash & Sage Soup
operations.subtitle: Autumn in a bowl
operations.description: Deeply roasted squash blended silky-smooth with fresh sage — a natural home for the garden harvest.

instructions.title: Roast
instructions.instruction: Toss squash and onion with oil, spread on a tray and roast until caramelised at the edges.

instructions.title: Crisp the sage
instructions.instruction: Fry sage leaves in a little oil for 30 seconds until crisp; set a few aside for garnish.

instructions.title: Blend
instructions.instruction: Simmer the roasted vegetables in stock for 10 minutes, add most of the sage, then blend until completely smooth. Season, adding maple syrup if the squash needs help.

operations.eoeNotes: Completely smooth once blended — a reliable EoE-friendly texture.
operations.antiInflammatoryNotes: Squash and olive oil; skip the maple syrup to keep sugar minimal.
operations.freezer: Freeze flat in bags for 6 months.
operations.reheating: Stovetop over medium, whisking as it warms.

operations.title: Tancook Island Fish Chowder
operations.subtitle: The way the coast makes it
operations.description: A simple Nova Scotia chowder — haddock, potatoes, and cream, finished with chives. No flour, no fuss.

instructions.title: Build the base
instructions.instruction: Melt butter in a heavy pot; sweat onion and celery until translucent, about 6 minutes.

instructions.title: Cook the potatoes
instructions.instruction: Add potatoes and just enough water to cover. Simmer until tender, about 12 minutes.

instructions.title: Poach the fish
instructions.instruction: Add milk, cream, and the fish in large pieces. Poach gently below a simmer until the fish flakes, 8–10 minutes. Never boil.

instructions.title: Finish
instructions.instruction: Season generously with salt and pepper. Rest 10 minutes off the heat, then serve scattered with chives.

operations.notes: Chowder improves with a rest — make it an hour ahead if you can.
operations.eoeNotes: Dairy is a common EoE trigger — swap milk/cream for oat cream if needed.
operations.storage: Fridge 2 days; the fish is best fresh.
operations.reheating: Very gently on the stove; do not boil.

operations.title: Garden Greek Salad
operations.subtitle: No lettuce, all crunch
operations.description: Tomatoes, cucumber and herbs straight from the garden with olives and a sharp oregano dressing.

instructions.instruction: Layer tomatoes, cucumber, onion and olives in a wide bowl — don't toss yet.
Whisk oil, vinegar, oregano and a pinch of salt; pour over the vegetables.
Top with feta (a slab, Greek-style), grind over pepper, and bring to the table untossed.

operations.bloodSugarNotes: Very low glycemic load — a good lunch anchor.
operations.antiInflammatoryNotes: Olive oil, tomatoes and herbs make this a Mediterranean classic.
operations.storage: Best immediately; keeps a day undressed.

operations.title: Blueberry Overnight Oats
operations.subtitle: Breakfast that makes itself
operations.description: Steel-cut texture without the morning wait — oats, chia and wild Nova Scotia blueberries.

instructions.instruction: Stir everything together in a jar. Really — that's it.
Refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight. Loosen with a splash of milk before eating.

operations.bloodSugarNotes: Oats + chia give a slow release; skip the maple syrup for the gentlest curve.
